 import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Quarter": [
        "2022-Q1", "2022-Q2", "2022-Q3", "2022-Q4",
        "2023-Q1", "2023-Q2", "2023-Q3", "2023-Q4",
        "2024-Q1", "2024-Q2", "2022-Q1", "2022-Q2",
        "2022-Q3", "2022-Q4", "2023-Q1", "2023-Q2",
        "2023-Q3", "2023-Q4", "2024-Q1", "2024-Q2",
        "2022-Q1", "2022-Q2", "2022-Q3", "2022-Q4",
        "2023-Q1", "2023-Q2", "2023-Q3", "2023-Q4"
    ],
    "Factor": [
        "Enterprise Corp", "Enterprise Corp", "Enterprise Corp", "Enterprise Corp",
        "Mid-Market Inc", "Mid-Market Inc", "Mid-Market Inc", "Mid-Market Inc",
        "Small Business LLC", "Small Business LLC",
        "Tech Innovators", "Tech Innovators", "Tech Innovators", "Tech Innovators",
        "Finance Leaders", "Finance Leaders", "Finance Leaders", "Finance Leaders",
        "Manufacturing Co", "Manufacturing Co",
        "Global Retail", "Global Retail", "Global Retail", "Global Retail",
        "NA Operations", "NA Operations", "NA Operations", "NA Operations"
    ],
    "Productivity Impact (k USD)": [
        28.5, 30.1, 29.3, 31.7,
        18.2, 19.6, 20.4, 17.9,
        -5.2, -4.1, 22.1, 23.8,

        26.2, 25.9, 8.1, 9.3,
        -3.8, -4.5, -2.9, -3.6,
        26.7, 27.2, 25.8, 28.9
    ],
    "Impact Type": [
        "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact",
        "Moderate Impact", "Moderate Impact", "Moderate Impact", "Moderate Impact",
        "Negative Impact", "Negative Impact",
        "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact",
        "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact",
        "Moderate Impact", "Moderate Impact",
        "Negative Impact", "Negative Impact", "Negative Impact", "Negative Impact",
        "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact", "High Impact"
    ],
    "Category": [
        "Company Scale", "Company Scale", "Company Scale", "Company Scale",
        "Company Scale", "Company Scale", "Company Scale", "Company Scale",
        "Company Scale", "Company Scale",
        "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment",
        "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment",
        "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment",
        "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment", "Industry Segment",
        "Geographic Region", "Geographic Region", "Geographic Region", "Geographic Region"
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df["Time"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Quarter"].apply(lambda x: f"{x[:4]}-{x[5:].replace('Q', '')}-01"))

fig = px.density_contour(
    df,
    x="Productivity Impact (k USD)",
    y="Category",
    color="Factor",
    marginal_x="violin",
    marginal_y="histogram",
    title="Density of Productivity Impact by Business Factor (k USD)",
    labels={"Productivity Impact (k USD)": "Productivity Impact (k USD)", "Category": "Factor"},
    category_orders={"Category": ["Company Scale", "Industry Segment", "Geographic Region"]},
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.G10,
    height=700,
    width=1000
)

fig.update_layout(
    legend_title_text="Business Factors",
    legend=dict(
        orientation="h",
        yanchor="bottom",
        y=1.02,
        xanchor="right",
        x=1
    ),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=50, b=50, t=80),
    title_font_size=20,
    font=dict(size=12)
)

fig.update_layout(showlegend=False)
fig.write_image("output.png")
SUMMARY
 The chart presented is a **density contour plot** combined with marginal violin plots and histograms, illustrating the density of productivity impact (measured in thousands of USD) across different business factors. The title of the chart, "Density of Productivity Impact by Business Factors (k USD)," indicates its focus on how productivity impacts vary by key business dimensions. The horizontal axis represents the **Productivity Impact (k USD)**, ranging from approximately -30,000 to 50,000 USD, while the vertical axis categorizes the data into three **Business Dimensions**: Company Scale, Industry Segment, and Geographic Region.

Each business factor is represented by a distinct color and labeled in the legend at the top of the chart. The **Company Scale** dimension includes Enterprise Corp (peach), Mid-Market Inc (light purple), and Small Business LLC (light pink). The **Industry Segment** dimension features Tech Innovators (teal), Finance Leaders (dark blue), and Manufacturing Co (purple). The **Geographic Region** dimension comprises Global Retail (orange) and NA Operations (green). The contour lines depict the density of productivity impacts within these categories, with tighter contours indicating higher concentrations of data points.

In the **Company Scale** dimension, Enterprise Corp displays a high concentration of productivity impacts around 28,000 to 32,000 USD, while Mid-Market Inc clusters around 18,000 to 20,000 USD. Small Business LLC, however, shows a negative productivity impact, concentrated around -5,000 USD. For the **Industry Segment**, Tech Innovators and Finance Leaders exhibit high productivity impacts, clustering around 22,000 to 28,000 USD, while Manufacturing Co has a moderate impact around 8,000 to 9,000 USD. In the **Geographic Region** dimension, Global Retail demonstrates a negative productivity impact around -4,000 USD, whereas NA Operations shows a high impact around 26,000 to 29,000 USD.

The marginal violin plots on the top provide a distribution overview of productivity impacts for each business factor, illustrating the spread and density of values. The marginal histograms on the right offer a proportional breakdown of each business dimension, showing the relative frequency of company scales, industry segments, and geographic regions within the dataset. The combination of these elements provides a comprehensive view of how productivity impacts are distributed across various business factors.
